_meta.indication: Replacement of endogenous growth hormone (GH) in adults with growth hormone deficiency (GHD).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled (double blind) and active-controlled (Norditropin, open label) 34-week trial; randomized 2:2:1 to somapacitan-beco, Norditropin, or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with growth hormone deficiency (AGHD) who were treatment-naïve to rhGH.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to end of main trial period (Week 34) in trunk fat percentage (TFP) assessed by DXA.
pivotal_trials.n: 301 subjects randomized (FAS: 120 SOGROYA, 61 placebo, 119 daily somatropin/Norditropin)
pivotal_trials.result: SOGROYA was superior to placebo for truncal fat % change at 34 weeks: -1.06% for SOGROYA vs +0.47% for placebo; absolute treatment difference -1.53% (95% CI -2.68, -0.38); p=0.0090. Daily somatropin achieved -2.23%.

nct_ctgov.title: Trial to Compare the Efficacy and Safety of NNC0195-0092 (Somapacitan) With Placebo and Norditropin® FlexPro® (Somatropin) in Adults With Growth Hormone Deficiency.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>2% and more frequent than placebo) included back pain (10% vs 3.3% placebo), arthralgia (6.7% vs 1.6%), dyspepsia (5% vs 3.3%). In the review, most common AEs were nasopharyngitis (20% vs 14.8% placebo). Class risks include headache, edema, intracranial hypertension, adrenal insufficiency, hyperglycemia, and neoplasms.
target_moa: Somapacitan-beco is a long-acting recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) derivative with an albumin-binding moiety; it binds to a dimeric GH receptor in the cell membrane of target cells resulting in intracellular signal transduction and pharmacodynamic effects mediated in part by IGF-I.
modality: Peptide/protein — long-acting recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) derivative with a non-covalent albumin-binding moiety.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions.

summary.text: Sogroya (somapacitan-beco) received traditional (full) approval via a standard-review BLA received August 28, 2019, approved August 2020 based on a single Phase 3 placebo-controlled trial (Study 4054) demonstrating superiority over placebo in trunk fat percentage; the application was not referred to an advisory committee, and deferred pediatric studies were required under PREA.

citations.quote: The Applicant demonstrated, in a single adequate and well-controlled trial carried out in adults with GHD that somapacitan-beco significantly reduced baseline trunk fat percentage (TFP) compared to placebo at the end of 34 weeks.

Your application for Sogroya was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the biologic in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of a disease.
We are deferring submission of your pediatric studies because this product is ready for approval for use in adults and the pediatric studies have not been completed.

requirement.text: 3890-1: Complete ongoing study NN8640-4172, a 1-year phase 2 randomized, open-label, active-control, dose-finding trial of once-weekly somapacitan versus daily Norditropin in pre-pubertal children with GHD, with single-arm safety follow-up periods.

citations.quote: 3890-1 Complete ongoing study NN8640-4172, a 1-year phase 2, randomized, open-label, active-control, dose-finding trial, to investigate efficacy and safety of once-weekly somapacitan versus daily Norditropin (somatropin) in pre-pubertal children with Growth Hormone Deficiency (GHD) (boys \ge 2.5 and \le 10 years of age, and girls \ge 2.5 and \le 9 years of age) followed by a 2-year single-arm period to evaluate safety in this cohort, and a 4-year single-arm period that also enrolls cohorts of younger children with GHD (boys and girls < 2.5 years of age) and older children with GHD (boys > 10 and \le 17 years of age, and girls > 9 and \le 17 years of age) to evaluate safety in all three cohorts.

requirement.text: 3890-2: Complete ongoing study NN8640-4263, a 1-year phase 3 randomized, parallel group, open-label trial of once-weekly somapacitan versus daily Norditropin in pre-pubertal pediatric patients with GHD, followed by a 3-year single-arm extension to evaluate long-term safety.

citations.quote: 3890-2 Complete ongoing study NN8640-4263, a 1-year phase 3 randomized, parallel group, open-label trial, to evaluate the efficacy and safety of once weekly somapacitan versus daily Norditropin (somatropin) in pre-pubertal pediatric patients (boys \ge 2.5 and \le 10 years of age, and girls \ge 2.5 and \le 9 years of age) with GHD, followed by a 3-year single-arm extension period to evaluate long-term safety.
